claims.quote: "We shall keep the household flexible," he said, and when the Queen looked at him he added, quieter, "The kitchen will have a small cold tray ready should Your Majesty return hungry."
"Sliced cold chicken, open sandwiches and fruit," the head cook recited and wrapped the tray in brown paper, folding the paper so that nothing showed.

supersedes.reason: aligned phrasing to the canonical menu recorded earlier; no menu change intended.

claims.quote: "The lady-in-waiting offered her support and discretion, as she had at the walk."
"The assistant ran like a second shadow: first to the kitchens where a head cook...then across the back passages to the stable-yard and back with notes folded small."

"In the stable-yard the driver was told to leave the curtains drawn and to hold the saloon in the shadow of the larches," the assistant repeated, as if the place were a line in a list of things that should not be noticed.

"He took the ledger and wrote a two-line list, scoring it with the economy of someone who believed in decisions that could be read across rooms: first the footman, then the kitchen, then the assistant, then the stable-yard, then the lady-in-waiting, then the press liaison."
"When the tray arrived the Queen lifted the cloth a little and smiled as if alone in a room that had always been hers."

promises.promise: Only those who must be told about the Queen's private movements will be informed.
promises.quote: "Only those who must know. No one else."
